title: Anrok vs. Sphere: Pricing, Features, & Which Is Right for You
summary: Compare Anrok and Sphere for pricing, features, customer support, and everything else you need to know to decide which is right for you.
body_markdown:
Anrok and Sphere are seen as comparable tax solutions because both are digital-first compliance products designed primarily for the SaaS market. However, the products differ in key ways, including industry longevity, pricing structure, and global reach.


**Anrok stands out for** its more native integrations, and its Custom plan includes features enterprise organizations want, including SSO, e-invoicing, multi-entity management, and audit-ready reporting. Anrok also provides automated support across over 150 countries.


**Sphere may be a better fit for** those seeking stronger customer support, as the company promises a 24/7 Slack channel and a dedicated account manager for Growth plan customers.


While Sphere serves only 130+ countries compared to Anrok's 150, its proprietary Tax Review and Assessment Model (TRAM) is an innovative AI solution for researching global indirect tax obligations that helps it stand apart.


This guide provides insight into the features, functionality, and pricing of each service so you can decide which is best for you. We’ll also talk about where both fall short and cover lighter-weight alternatives that may be a better fit for ecommerce companies.


## Anrok vs. Sphere overview


If you are deciding between Anrok and Sphere, the table below provides an overview of key features of each service:


Anrok Sphere


Built for SaaS and remote-first companies with a need for strong HR integrations SaaS and digital businesses with global customers


Founded/launched 2020 2021; came out of stealth in 2024


Starting price $100 per market per month $100 per region per month (under 10 regions)


Higher tier Custom tier has quote-based pricing Growth plan (10+ regions) has quote-based pricing


Per-filing or per-registration fees No No


International coverage 150+ countries 130+ countries


G2 reviews 4.5/5 (308 reviews as of this writing) 5/5 (33 reviews as of this writing)


Sphere and Anrok have many similarities, although Anrok is more established and serves more countries.


However, Sphere's TRAM and AI-native focus may appeal to companies that want a compliance solution that harnesses AI research tools to provide constant, comprehensive automated monitoring of regulatory shifts.

## Anrok vs. Sphere Pricing


Both Anrok and Sphere charge a monthly subscription fee by region rather than by specific compliance task.


However, the cost structures vary, so the most affordable option may differ based on business size, number of registrations, and filing volume.


### Anrok pricing


Anrok offers two tiers of service:


- **Starter:** For $100 per month per market, Anrok provides AI tax intelligence, global exposure monitoring, real-time tax calculation, filing and remittance, exemption certificate management, and physical nexus tracking. A market is a single jurisdiction where a company has registration and tax obligations.
- **Custom:** You must get a quote to learn the price. Custom adds e-invoicing, advanced integrations, multi-billing and multi-entity management, enhanced exemption certificate management, audit-ready reporting, global tax consultants, reconciliation tools, an address resolution API, SSO, and priority support.


Anrok notes that sellers on the Starter plan with high transaction volumes may be subject to additional fees to cover third-party costs that Anrok incurs.


### Sphere pricing


Sphere also offers two service tiers, but the number of regions can determine which tier you are in, although you also have the option to move up to Growth sooner:


- **Starter:** For $100 per region per month, Sphere offers monitoring, registration, calculation for up to 50,000 transactions, filing and remittance, and local integrations.
- **Growth:** This tier is priced by quote. Once you reach 10+ regions, you must transition to custom pricing. It includes everything in Starter, a dedicated account manager, a tax team on demand, and 24/7 support. You can also get help with back tax calculations at no extra cost.
- **Add-ons:** Input tax recovery for[value-added tax (VAT)](https://www.numeral.com/blog/vat-compliance) and goods and services tax (GST) is an add-on service offered, as is e-invoicing. You will need to obtain a custom quote if you want to use these services.


Like Anrok, Sphere charges more at high volume: a flat per-transaction fee once you pass 50,000 transactions. Sphere also passes along any registration fees a jurisdiction charges.


## Anrok vs. Sphere Features


### Tax calculation and taxability


- Both Anrok and Sphere help you determine whether an item is taxed and at what rates.
- Both services focus on supporting SaaS customers and have processes in place to manage the complexity of indirect taxes on SaaS, including challenges raised by[subscription billing](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-for-subscription-businesses) and the disparate treatment of[digital goods](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) across states.


Key differences between the two include:


- **Integration with billing and revenue systems:** Anrok integrates with more billing and revenue systems than Sphere.
- **Global reach:** Anrok can manage[global tax compliance](https://www.numeral.com/blog/global-vat-compliance-for-saas-and-software-companies) in slightly more countries than Sphere (150+ vs. 130+).
- **Dedicated customer service:** Sphere offers more comprehensive customer support for companies in its highest-service tier, including 24/7 support via Slack.
- **Cutting-edge research tools:** TRAM automatically collects and interprets any administrative or legislative rulings or guidance, uses this information to build product taxonomies, and determines taxability, rates, and sourcing rules across jurisdictions.


### Nexus tracking and monitoring


[Nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) means you have sufficient connections within a state that you must collect sales tax on their behalf.


For SaaS companies, this is harder to track than it sounds. Subscription renewals and usage-based billing can push you past a state's threshold mid-year, even if nothing about how you sell has changed.


You could establish[economic nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) or[physical nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) , with economic nexus determined by volume or number of transactions and physical nexus by a physical presence, such as storing goods or having a local storefront.


Both Anrok and Sphere offer tracking for both types of nexus. Monitoring for economic nexus requires tracking sales in each state across all storefronts and billing platforms, while monitoring for physical nexus can require integrations with inventory-management or HR tools.


Both Anrok and Sphere also include nexus monitoring in their Starter and Custom/Growth services. However, there are some critical differences:


- **Free nexus monitoring:** Sphere offers free nexus monitoring. You pay for Sphere's service only after you register and begin collecting and filing. Anrok does not offer free monitoring.
- **Integrations:** Because Anrok offers more integrations, it may be easier to connect all of your relevant platforms to Anrok for monitoring.


Both companies also monitor for regulatory changes that could affect nexus. For example,[California recently passed SB 122](https://www.numeral.com/blog/california-sb-122) that makes most forms of SaaS taxable starting Jan. 1, 2027.


## Registrations, filings, and support


Once you trigger nexus in any state, you must[register with its revenue department](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-permit-registration) and begin collecting, filing, and remitting taxes.


Both Anrok and Sphere can register on your behalf, and registration is included as part of your service. Each new region or market where you register adds to your monthly costs. However, there are some important differences between the two:


- Once you reach 10 regions, you will need to switch to the Growth tier with Sphere. Anrok does not have this strict threshold that triggers different pricing.
- Anrok has received a notable number of complaints in[G2 reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/anrok/reviews?qs=pros-and-cons&filters%5Bcomment_answer_values%5D=VAT&order=g2_default&utf8=%E2%9C%93#cons) about the complexity and challenges of its registration service. Sphere has largely received more favorable reviews, but has many fewer reviews.

## Choosing between Anrok and Sphere


Anrok and Sphere both have their own strengths and weaknesses. Here's how to decide which of the two is right for you:


**Anrok is a top choice for:**


- Companies that want a more established platform with a larger base of independent reviews
- Enterprise organizations that need additional services such as e-invoicing and robust audit-ready reporting
- Companies with a large global presence due to Anrok offering support in more countries
- Companies that require more integrations, especially with popular billing tools like Stripe, NetSuite, and QuickBooks


**Sphere is a top choice for:**


- Companies that need cutting-edge compliance monitoring services using TRAM
- Early adopters who are comfortable with a newer platform with fewer proven reviews
- Businesses that prioritize customer service and need 24/7 support
- Companies that want nexus monitoring before making a commitment


You should explore both options carefully to see which is a better fit.


## Where both platforms fall short


Both Sphere and Anrok have some areas where they fall short, including:


- **No comprehensive free nexus monitoring:** Anrok does not offer[free nexus monitoring](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) . Sphere provides free monitoring until you register. However, Sphere may not be comprehensive since it may lack native integrations with your key sales channels or billing solutions.
- **You're locked into monthly fees:** You pay per market or region, rather than when work is actually performed. By contrast,[Numeral charges](https://www.numeral.com/pricing) $75 per filing and $150 per registration with no commitment required.
- **Registration challenges:** Customers of both companies have reported various challenges, including that some parts of the process require manual input.
- **No guarantee:** Neither Sphere nor Anrok provides a guarantee that filing will be on time or that you will be audit-ready. Liability for compliance ultimately lies with you.

## Anrok vs Sphere FAQs


Still need to know more? Here are the answers to some frequently asked questions about Anrok vs. Sphere.


### Is Anrok or Sphere better for a SaaS company?


Anrok has a longer history of providing sales tax support and has more integrations to make operations easier. Sphere is a modern alternative with an AI-first approach and a unique compliance tool that helps monitor regulatory changes worldwide.


### How much does Sphere cost?


Sphere costs $100 per region per month for under 10 regions. For customers with 10 or more regions who switch to the Growth tier, pricing is customized. There are no per-filing fees on either the Starter or Growth tier.


### How much does Anrok cost?


Anrok costs $100 per market per month. For more advanced services, including e-invoicing, custom pricing is available.


### What's the difference between Anrok and Sphere?


There are numerous differences between Anrok and Sphere:


- Anrok is more established.
- Anrok has more integrations.
- Anrok supports your company in over 150 countries, while Sphere supports it in 130 countries.
- Sphere has more favorable customer reviews (although over a smaller audience base).
- Sphere has more comprehensive customer service.
- Sphere has a proprietary AI-powered tool for global compliance research.
- Sphere offers free nexus monitoring, and you pay only upon registration and filing.


Both services lack certain key features provided by competitors like Numeral. For example, neither service offers an on-time filing guarantee, which Numeral provides for peace of mind.


### Is Sphere a proven sales tax compliance platform?


Sphere was founded in 2021 but did not launch from stealth until late 2024. It has a shorter history and fewer independent reviews than more established competitors. However, the reviews it does have are strongly positive.


### Do Anrok or Sphere charge per-filing fees?


Neither Sphere nor Anrok charges a per-filing fee. Both charge monthly per region/market, which means you pay for monthly service even if no filing is required during that time period.
